`onesie calibrate` asks a question about records whose right answer is already known, and prints
what each cut catches and what it flags by mistake. It never picks the cut. That is your call,
made from the report.

`-i` is jsonl, csv or tsv. `--map` picks the text the question reads, and a `--label` jq
expression takes the right answer from the same record:

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' \
    --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume < labelled.jsonl
```

A yes or no label is true, false, yes, no, 1 or 0 in any case. A pick or rate label is an option or
level name exactly as declared. A null, empty or missing label leaves the record out for that
question. A question file's `assert`, `abstain_if`, `threshold`, `min_confidence` and `fallback`
are ignored, so a gated file calibrates as it stands, while the same flags typed on the command
line exit 2.

The built in starter sets come calibrated already. `-f shell-safety` and the others that
`onesie questions` lists as `built in` ship with cuts measured on labelled records, so use one
as it stands before you write and calibrate a gate of your own.

For a flag this skill does not cover, run `onesie --help` or `onesie calibrate --help`, and `onesie -V` for the version and the built in limits.

## Rules

### Map only the text a person would read, never the label.

calibrate measures how well the question reads the text. A `--map` that passes the label field, or the whole record, lets the model read the answer and flatters every number in the report. `--label` runs on the whole record, not on the mapped state, so the label never has to be in the map. `--map` is required.

**Bad:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '{body, is_urgent}' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id'
```

**Good:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id'
```

### Always pass --out answers.jsonl --resume --id, so a relabel or new --cuts asks nothing.

`--out` keeps every answer as `-o json` lines, with a fingerprint in `answers.jsonl.onesie` beside it. `--resume` needs `--id`, and asks only the records the file does not answer, so fixing a label, adding labelled records or trying other `--cuts` asks nothing again for the records already answered. Pass `--resume` on the first run too, since a missing file starts fresh. A change to the questions, the model, the provider, `-i`, `--map` or `--id` makes the resume exit 2, so delete the file and its sidecar and ask again. A plain stream run can resume the same file, given the same questions, model, `-i`, `--map` and `--id`, with `-o json` and no gate or merge.

**Bad:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent'
```

**Good:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume
```

### Read the interval columns and the worst misses before you pick a cut.

For a yes or no question the report has one row per cut. A row flags a record when `value >= cut`, the same test `--threshold 0.8` and `--assert 'urgent.value >= 0.8'` apply, so the cut goes into the gate as written. `catches` is the share of labelled yes records flagged, `false alarms` the share of labelled no records flagged, and `right when flagged` the share of flagged records labelled yes. Each shows the count, the share and its 95 percent interval, and on a few records the interval is the part to read: `2/2 100% 34-100%` says little. `worst misses` lists by id the records answered furthest from their label, each with the start of its mapped text on one line. Read them: a wrong label is fixed in the data, and a real miss means the question needs rewording and another calibration. A pick or rate question reports its agreement, a table of labelled against picked, and one row per confidence cut with the share it answers and their agreement, which is where a `--min-confidence` comes from. The cuts run from 0.05 to 0.95 in steps of 0.05, and `--cuts 0.5,0.7,0.9` names your own.

**Bad:**

```sh
onesie --ask urgent='is this urgent' --threshold 0.9 -i jsonl --map '.body' --id '.id'
```

**Good:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --cuts 0.5,0.7,0.9 --out answers.jsonl --resume
```

### Gate the calibration with --require, using lower() or upper() on a small sample.

`--require` turns the report into a check. The report still prints, each requirement that did not hold is named on stderr, and the run exits 1. A requirement reads `[lower|upper](ID.MEASURE) OP NUMBER [at CUT]`. The measures are `catches`, `false_alarms`, `right_when_flagged` and `auc` for a yes or no question, `agreement` for pick and rate, and `within_one` for rate. NUMBER is a fraction, so `95` exits 2. On a few records the plain value passes on luck, since 16 of 16 reads 100 percent. `lower()` compares the low end of the 95 percent interval instead, 81 percent for 16 of 16, so `lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9` fails until there are enough labelled records to back it. `lower` takes `>=` or `>`, `upper` takes `<=` or `<`, as in `upper(urgent.false_alarms) <= 0.1 at 0.9`, and `auc` has no interval. Without `at`, the cut comes from the `-f` file's `assert` when it compares `ID.value < X` or `ID.value >= X`, and `at abstain` takes it from the file's `abstain_if`. A missing cut exits 2 before any request.

**Bad:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume --require 'urgent.catches >= 0.95 at 0.9'
```

**Good:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume --require 'lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9 at 0.9'
```

### In CI, commit the answers file and its .onesie sidecar, run --offline, and pin -m, plus --provider when it matters.

`--offline`, with `--out` and `--resume`, reads every answer from the file and asks nothing, so the check needs no key, costs nothing and never rewrites the file. A record the file does not answer, a missing file or a fingerprint that does not match exits 2. In CI that means the questions or the records changed, so rerun without `--offline` and commit the new file. The fingerprint names the model and the provider, so pin a versioned model such as `-m jev-1.13.0`, since an alias such as `jev-latest` moves on release. Pin `--provider` too when `ONESIE_PROVIDER` can differ between the machine that wrote the file and CI. `--offline` is refused beside `--mock`, `--print-request` and `--prune`.

**Bad:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume --require 'lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9 at 0.9'
```

**Good:**

```sh
onesie calibrate --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --map '.body' --label urgent='.is_urgent' --id '.id' -m jev-1.13.0 --provider typesafe --out answers.jsonl --resume --offline --require 'lower(urgent.catches) >= 0.9 at 0.9'
```
